items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: Johnny Lindsey would be sitting up behind the bass and they'd think it was me.

ctx.x: Yeah, we got Harvey Liferbuss on the boat at first when we were on another trombone player. We got Zoo Robertson and they got Johnny Lindsey. That's when they used to come on the boat. Johnny Lindsey would be sitting up behind the bass and they'd think it was me. We looked a whole lot alike. Did he play bass or did he play trombone? We played trombone and bass.
The Stratford's people they liked it, Johnny and George, very much. They liked it.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: John Lindsay and I looked so much alike people didn't know what it is that Johnny Reed was me playing sometimes

ctx.x: It was around 1997 and 1999 when my brother bought that big bass for me. Uh-huh. He had left working for McCall's and he started working with a little band, a guy called Roy Palmer. Roy Palmer, yes. Roy Palmer was our guitar player. You had to see what became a trombone player? No, let me see what Roy was playing. Roy was playing trumpet. Uh-huh. And Joe Johnson was our guitar player. So Joe Johnson learned trumpet and Roy Palmer and Roy Palmer was good too. Joe died. That's what I tell the guys, they read about…
Sure. Why would you play? Bass drum?
